ctor.rationale: `base(1, CardType.Power, CardRarity.Uncommon, TargetType.Self)` (FeelNoPain.cs:24-27) == cost 1 / POWER / UNCOMMON / SELF. It does NOT override GainsBlock -- cards/base.py:65-69 calls this out by name: "Feel No Pain's number belongs to its power, not the card" -- and the sim correctly leaves `gains_block` False.

CanonicalVars.issue: `new DynamicVar("Power", 3m)` (FeelNoPain.cs:16) is a generic power var, and the sim stores it in **`_block`** -- the attribute `Card.base_block` reads (cards/base.py:202-205). So the sim reports Feel No Pain as a card that itself grants 3 block, which is exactly the confusion cards/base.py:65-69 warns about when it explains why `gains_block` cannot be derived from `base_block`. The card grants NO block; FeelNoPainPower does, on exhaust. This is worse than the ordinary inlined-var finding: it is not a missing number but a WRONG one. `full_env.card_features` writes both `base_block` and `preview_card_block(s, card)` into the observation (full_env.py:483-485), so a policy is told Feel No Pain gives 3 (later 4) block on play. DORMANT for game fidelity -- `on_play` passes the same value to the power, so combat behaviour is identical, and no gameplay code reads `base_block` -- but LIVE for the observation encoder. The correct storage is `_plating`-style: card/eternal_armor stores the same shape of number in `_plating` and reports it through `magic_number` instead.

OnPlay.rationale: `PowerCmd.Apply<FeelNoPainPower>(choiceContext, Owner.Creature, DynamicVars["Power"].BaseValue, Owner.Creature, this)` (FeelNoPain.cs:31) == `PowerCmd.apply(ctx.hooks, ctx.player, FeelNoPainPower, self._block, applier=ctx.player)`. The VALUE handed to the power is right on both sides; only where the sim stores it is wrong.
